props.title: Funny Face
props.initialSlug: Fashion meets philosophy in Parisian romance

sections.content: **Funny Face** (1957) represents the perfect fusion of Hollywood glamour, fashion, and musical sophistication. Fred Astaire plays fashion photographer Dick Avery (based on real-life legend Richard Avedon, who consulted on the film) opposite Audrey Hepburn's intellectual bookstore clerk turned model. Director Stanley Donen, fresh off **Singin' in the Rain** (1952), brings his characteristic visual flair and impeccable timing to this Gershwin-scored spectacular. The film's stunning use of color photography, particularly in the fashion sequences, revolutionized how style could be captured on screen, influencing later works like **Blow-Up** (1966) and **The Devil Wears Prada** (2006).

sections.content: The Paris sequences in **Funny Face** showcase a pivotal moment in American cinema's love affair with the City of Light. Following the success of **An American in Paris** (1951), Hollywood increasingly used Paris as more than just a backdrop - it became a character itself. The film's integration of real Parisian locations with studio sets created a template followed by countless films, from **Charade** (1963) to **Midnight in Paris** (2011). Hepburn's famous impromptu dance in the smoky underground café captures both the fantasy and reality of American perceptions of French bohemian culture. SUBHEAD: Fashion in Film

**Funny Face** marked a watershed moment in the relationship between cinema and haute couture. Legendary costume designer Edith Head collaborated with Givenchy to create Hepburn's iconic wardrobe, establishing a partnership that would continue through films like **Breakfast at Tiffany's** (1961). The famous "Think Pink!" sequence satirizes yet celebrates fashion magazine culture, predating similar treatments in **The Devil Wears Prada** (2006) and **Zoolander** (2001). The film's innovative fashion photography sequences, with their bold colors and abstract compositions, influenced both cinema and fashion photography for decades.
